headline: Meta's own research finds Muse shops the open web, not the Shopify catalogue it was meant to read
intro: Back after a 15-day gap in the landing pipeline (fixed today, see below) — three real developments since the 28 Sep edition, not a recap padded to cover the silence.

items.title: Profound: Muse fills most of its shopping picks from the open web, not the merchant catalogue
items.what: Profound's own test of Meta's Muse shopping agent found it filled 4 of its 6 product recommendations from the open web and only 2 from Meta's product catalogue — even though the catalogue returned roughly 60 candidate products from 30 merchants, about 15x more options than the web picks it actually used. Neither Muse nor rival agent Instinct identifies itself when browsing; both present as an ordinary visitor. A follow-up Profound post on 8 Oct, based on an instruction file it says it extracted from Muse (its own caveat: may be stale since late September), reports the agent is told to rank well-known merchants first and check no more than three open-web stores per request.
items.sowhat: Complicates the 28 Sep edition's framing that Muse shops the Shopify catalogue, not the feed we optimise — the catalogue clearly isn't winning the recommendation even when a merchant is eligible for it. For any US-facing client on Shopify (check Reiss US, Superdry US), general on-site content and open-web visibility may matter to Muse at least as much as the Shopify Catalog feed. Flag as 'unproven and Meta-side' rather than act on — nothing here is a lever we control yet.

items.title: ChatGPT adds virtual try-on and a saved-items Favorites library to shopping
items.what: OpenAI added a 'Try On' button to ChatGPT shopping results: a shopper uploads or takes a selfie (or screenshots an item from another site) and sees it composited onto their own photo, built on the ChatGPT Images 2.5 model, alongside a Favorites library for saving products into folders. Live on mobile and web; reference photos are stored for reuse unless deleted in settings.
items.sowhat: A visual, apparel-specific surface with no published feed-side lever yet — OpenAI hasn't said how a retailer's own product imagery factors into the render, and there's no stated opt-in/opt-out. Relevant to every apparel client (Reiss, Superdry, Schuh, Monsoon/Accessorize) as a 'clients will ask about this' line this quarter, not a brief yet.

items.title: Anthropic published a commerce-agent blueprint — agents built ON Claude for a retailer's own site, not a shopping surface inside Claude
items.what: Anthropic released 'commerce-agents' (Apache 2.0): reference code for a customer-facing shopping agent and an operator-facing merchant agent that a retailer builds into its own app or site — not a consumer shopping feature inside Claude itself. Shopify published example code applying it to a live Shopify store; Accenture, Mastercard and Visa are named partners, and checkout/payment stay with the retailer's own stack. Anthropic cites larger carts and higher completion among early users — its own figures, not independently verified.
items.sowhat: Backfilled here — it predates this edition's window but never reached a digest, since the pipeline that would have carried it broke the same week it shipped. Directly relevant to how we position Tachyon: this is Anthropic's own house view of what a 'good' commerce agent looks like, worth reading before the next AI-readiness conversation even though no client is building on it.
